newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NASA says Mir repairs could be left to new crew.
newsitem.headline: NASA says Mir repairs could be left to new crew.

text.p: Vital repairs originally scheduled for the end of this week to restore power to the damaged Mir space station might be delayed until a relief crew arrives in early August, a NASA official said on Tuesday.

"We will also discuss with the Russians the urgency of this EVA (extra vehicular activity) against the potential of slipping it to some other Mir crew," Philip Engelauf told reporters at Mission Control outside Moscow when asked if the NASA astronaut now aboard Mir might stand in for the ailing Russian commander.

Commander Vasily Tsibliyev was due to don a spacesuit and carry out electrical repairs in the punctured, airless Spektr module with flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin nearby. But Tsibliyev has developed a possibly stress-related heart problem, throwing the schedule of repairs in doubt.
Russian officials said British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale, the other member of the three-man crew, might be asked to step in and take Tsibliyev's place, but have yet to take a decision.
"The decision has not yet been made and will probably not be made for at least 24-48 hours, possibly longer," Engelauf said. "We're just going to take our time."

He said NASA and the Russians would be looking at Foale's training records to help determine whether he had had the full relevant preparation for using a Russian spacesuit in the particular configuration needed during the planned repairs.
